term: Source Separation and Target Speaker Extraction
definition: Separating overlapped speakers in a mixture (the cocktail party problem), or extracting only a target speaker conditioned on an enrollment embedding of their voice.
details: Separating overlapped speakers in a mixture (the cocktail party problem), or extracting only a target speaker conditioned on an enrollment embedding of their voice. The key technology behind meeting transcription with overlap and personalized ASR.

explainer.lead: It is the task of separating overlapped speakers in a mixture, or extracting only a target speaker given an enrollment embedding of their voice. It is the key technology behind meeting transcription with overlap and personalized ASR.

tiers.eli5: When several people talk at once, this pulls apart the voices, or picks out just the one person you enrolled by their voice.
tiers.practitioner: It enables meeting transcription when speakers overlap and personalized speech recognition aimed at one enrolled voice. The pitfall is conditioning on a weak or noisy enrollment embedding, which degrades extraction of the target.
tiers.paperLevel: Two related problems: separating overlapped speakers in a mixture (the cocktail party problem), and extracting a target speaker conditioned on an enrollment embedding of their voice. No formal formula or bound is given.

explainer.example: A meeting recorder separates two people talking over each other, then uses a short enrollment clip to pull out only the enrolled participant's speech.
